title: The Clever Tortoise and the Rain

pages.text: It had not rained for many weeks. The grass turned yellow and the river dried into a thin brown stream. All the animals were thirsty.
sentences: It had not rained for many weeks.
The grass turned yellow and the river dried into a thin brown stream.
All the animals were thirsty.
pages.alt: A dry riverbed with a thin muddy stream, yellow grass and a few thirsty animals in the distance.

pages.text: Old Tortoise did not complain. Every day he walked slowly along the riverbank, and he watched everything. ‘If you look carefully,’ he liked to say, ‘the world will tell you its secrets.’
sentences: Old Tortoise did not complain.
Every day he walked slowly along the riverbank, and he watched everything.
‘If you look carefully,’ he liked to say, ‘the world will tell you its secrets.’
pages.alt: An old tortoise with a patterned shell walks slowly along a dry riverbank, looking all around.

pages.text: One morning he saw a long line of ants hurrying uphill. Each ant carried a tiny white egg. ‘Why are the ants moving to high ground?’ he wondered.
sentences: One morning he saw a long line of ants hurrying uphill.
Each ant carried a tiny white egg.
‘Why are the ants moving to high ground?’ he wondered.
pages.alt: A line of ants each carrying a small white egg climbs a slope while the tortoise watches.

pages.text: Then he saw the swallows flying low over the ground, and he smelled something sweet and damp in the wind. ‘Rain is coming,’ said Tortoise. ‘I am sure of it.’
sentences: Then he saw the swallows flying low over the ground, and he smelled something sweet and damp in the wind.
‘Rain is coming,’ said Tortoise.
‘I am sure of it.’
pages.alt: Swallows skim low over the grass as the tortoise lifts his head to smell the wind.

pages.text: He told the others. Hare laughed so hard he rolled in the dust. ‘The sky is empty!’ said Hare. ‘Tortoise is too slow to know anything!’ Only Heron listened quietly.
sentences: He told the others.
Hare laughed so hard he rolled in the dust.
‘The sky is empty!’ said Hare.
‘Tortoise is too slow to know anything!’ Only Heron listened quietly.
pages.alt: A hare rolls on the ground laughing while a tall heron listens quietly to the tortoise.

pages.text: ‘When the rain comes, it will run away down the hill,’ said Tortoise, ‘unless we dig a big hole to catch it. Then we will have water for many weeks.’ Heron nodded. ‘I will help.’
sentences: ‘When the rain comes, it will run away down the hill,’ said Tortoise, ‘unless we dig a big hole to catch it.
Then we will have water for many weeks.’ Heron nodded.
‘I will help.’
pages.alt: The tortoise draws a plan in the dust with his foot while the heron nods.

pages.text: Together they dug all afternoon. Slowly, other animals came to help, even the ants and the little birds. Hare watched for a while. Then, with a sigh, he picked up a stick and began to dig.
sentences: Together they dug all afternoon.
Slowly, other animals came to help, even the ants and the little birds.
Hare watched for a while.
Then, with a sigh, he picked up a stick and began to dig.
pages.alt: Many animals dig a wide round hole together in the dry ground; the hare joins in with a stick.

pages.text: That night the sky grew dark. Thunder rolled across the hills, and the rain came down hard. It ran down the slope and poured into the big hole. By morning, the hole was full of fresh, clear water.
sentences: That night the sky grew dark.
Thunder rolled across the hills, and the rain came down hard.
It ran down the slope and poured into the big hole.
By morning, the hole was full of fresh, clear water.
pages.alt: At night, rain falls hard on a hillside and water runs into a wide round pond-hole.

pages.text: Every animal drank as much as they needed. Hare came to Tortoise with his ears drooping. ‘I am sorry I laughed,’ he said. ‘You looked carefully, and I did not.’
sentences: Every animal drank as much as they needed.
Hare came to Tortoise with his ears drooping.
‘I am sorry I laughed,’ he said.
‘You looked carefully, and I did not.’
pages.alt: Hare apologises to the tortoise beside the full pond while other animals drink.

pages.text: Tortoise smiled. ‘Slow is not the same as wrong,’ he said. ‘And a hole dug by many hands holds more water than one dug alone.’ From then on, the animals always listened when Tortoise spoke. The end.
sentences: Tortoise smiled.
‘Slow is not the same as wrong,’ he said.
‘And a hole dug by many hands holds more water than one dug alone.’ From then on, the animals always listened when Tortoise spoke.
The end.
pages.alt: The tortoise smiles at the hare while the animals sit together by the pond at sunset.

activities.question: What clues told Tortoise that rain was coming?
options: Ants moving to high ground and low-flying swallows
activities.explanation: He noticed the ants carrying eggs uphill, the swallows flying low and the damp smell on the wind.

activities.question: Why did Hare begin to dig?
options: He saw that the others were working and wanted to help
He was told to by the king
activities.explanation: The text does not say it directly: we work it out from Hare watching and then sighing before he digs.

items: Tortoise notices the ants and swallows.
The animals dig a big hole together.
The rain fills the hole with water.

activities.prompt: Hare does not believe Tortoise. What do you think will happen next?
Hare said sorry. Think of a time you said sorry. How did it feel?

glossary.definition: The land along the side of a river.
Small birds that fly fast and often swoop low before rain.
Ground that goes up or down at an angle.
